### 2026-11-11: Starting off Cyberdeckie

**4h**

Starting off Cyberdeckie

![CyberdeckieSS0](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/be1e4e2161ed5d6665f3e3af10d1c16b83078403499ed9d4afde607e4dfb7f2b.png)
![Screenshot 2026-11-09 at 9.05.02 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/cc111fc4f7de558621f11b5a02ae28fec9f414e9461402afe6684ac0658addd9.png)
First off, I had to pick which parts to use for my cyberdeckie. It took a considerable amount of time to find everything. Managed to get most of the parts from lcsc, so that’s good! After that, i downloaded all of the datasheets so that i could refer to them when making the schematic.

![CyberdeckieSS1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/74bf030df7db6723df9b8418d9e142031642de3fe623f613df4ae13f68870ec0.png)
![CyberdeckieSS2](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/b63535db0581c10d96b573f7700ba5df39539bf234f320aa7e1378937f9d4a25.png)
Started on the schematic!! For this project, I made multiple pages, grouping them into RPi, Power, Display and Keyboard. Started with the Raspberry Pi and added the net labels.

### 2026-11-10: Making the schematic for power parts; the big learning point

**5.75h**

Making the schematic for power parts; the big learning point

![CyberdeckieSS3](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/3eb291c965b319aeed0b248cd423a5212e22db836e9c5876a145cbd6f8547fc9.png)
Started with the USB-C, which was quite straightforward. Referred to the datasheet pinout
Looking back now I actually accidentally added vbus as a net label, not a power symbol so I’ll go change that haha

![CyberdeckieSS5](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/a0e09283ebf8bd675fc530ab1c6a0bafee2786da2f26e1a1f600402eda70f245.png)
Got to the most tedious and challenging part of the schematic, the battery charger (BQ24074)… but i definitely did learn the most here.
So uhhhhh when i saw this my brain couldn’t even process it.. but! I tried to connect whatever I understood first, like connected the pins to the ground.

![CyberdeckieSS6](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/11798b5d76e2e0a135af7350b328473ccb8cccf1c75d29dede8d362640e0fd61.png)
And then came the mighty Google: understanding what the symbols stand for 🫣 i did end up using a diff pic cos this one wasn’t as helpful as the others
This was a great help. Well actually the datasheet did help a ton, especially after I understood it all. After that, i connected the capacitors (which were actually really easy I just didn’t know what they were at first), and then everything else came slowly.

![CyberdeckieSS7](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/b20fb7291c9e7d2b7083e5ae0219a351eae3069db7bf60baff36ce0715025d26.png)
Progress! Rough, but progress! Relied a LOT on the datasheet for this component. Also realised that since I was working with different pages, I had to use global net labels, so I switched them all!

![CyberdeckieSS8](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/e482fa33d2bfc97598d0e37690ae8ec3a7ef80ac45fdb818f18ddfd0b622a828.png)
After I kinda got everything, I ran the ERC and wow so many errors! Turns out something moved in my RPi page and a ton of labels weren’t connected so I moved them back and yayyyy settled :D

![CyberdeckieSS9](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/50b406332d364d96e1d49c2f6b8e4d792fe9463f598e334a6ea4a2986060aee9.png)
Lastly, I decided to clean up my power page and labels too bc some of them were kinda redundant. After that, everything was much neater :) Also added the necessary power flags and yay done with the power page fully!

Really didn’t expect to spend so so much time with this page but i definitely did learn a lot. In the end, a lot of time was spent finding which symbols and labels to connect with the pins and also fixing mistakes made.

10/11: Completing the schematic

After that, I ran the DRC to make sure everything was okay and yay omg no errors I love it! I also decided to run the 'annotate schematic' to make sure everything is labelled nicely and neatly :)

### 2026-11-11: 11/11: PCB Editing time!!!

**6.5h**

11/11: PCB Editing time!!!

It was finally time to update the schematic to the PCB!! Well, I was really really excited to move on to the PCB, so I totally forgot about the assigning of footprints so... yeah I ran into a bunch of errors when I tried to update the PCB. whoops!

![CyberdeckieSS16](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/e855850ee82571495fbe68daf83cd4f715165043bc09877d0c45359dda1f770b.png)
Updated and found all of the footprints! Had to search for and download a few but it wasn't too bad so yayy

![CyberdeckieSS17](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/315391bfd3630f919862fbd9e9a3cfa962df9e2f8d544dfffb441455734f5dc1.png)
Managed to updated the PCB from the schematic successfully!! But it wasn't a very pleasant surprise when I saw all of the components. I definitely did not see so many components before and I hadn't worked with these especially, so uh well it was new!

![CyberdeckieSS18](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/f86d25688727626395300c98a55cb5ef1d5d1a883ed1ccc1fbc5a3821f338b5a.png)
I first tried separating the key switches and arrange the keyboard since it was the main part of the PCB. Well, this one took sooooooooooo much time omg I was gonna take my brains out for this. Especially since everything had to be placed specifically, I had to find the different switches one by one while referring to the schematic for which SW to place down. Oh gosh, it really took a lot of time for arranging the PCB.

![Screenshot 2026-11-12 at 9.22.29 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/2bf50f8cee98062fbb5c2866da52d75fbc9dcaaf5426c05b483655abc8b2420b.png)
YAY progress! It was still a little messy but I was getting the hang of putting the different switches in place and tidying the row to be on the same level. Wasn't too sure on how to tidy the columns yet though heh

![Screenshot 2026-11-12 at 9.39.12 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/352921c8fed2fe3a71ec0468dffc4c57dd2fe7dec4d6750096cb482da1037cb6.png)
FINALLY DONE with placing all of the switches! And then came the diodes...

![Screenshot 2026-11-12 at 9.50.54 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/c18653a89644866f17a0e4f6c2eab2b0e1fc771238eb72000aebf325137700dd.png)
Actually forgot B.cu existed so I was like omg do I have to place the diodes right beside the switches? but nope luckily not because we love B.cu and it's so much neater that way. Love just having to place them in the middle of the switch! This one also took a while since I had to find the individual diodes for the specific switches. Glad I managed to get that done though!

![Screenshot 2026-11-12 at 11.06.47 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/a01f1793acb59e22c26c0dd9556678e739f3b70f8d1958f801eafd98548853e1.png)
After getting the base keyboard down, I added in the rest of the larger components like the FPC connector, RPi connector and battery stuff. Did not want to touch the power components bc I did not know how I was supposed to do those and they were so much smaller than I imagined.

### 2026-11-11: 11/11: Finishing up the PCB YAYYYY

**4h**

11/11: Finishing up the PCB YAYYYY

![Screenshot 2026-11-12 at 11.06.47 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/7e6f95be77bea47f5202057126684dd43daf8e3816404dea4ccda3149211e0e7.png)
First off, I added every single component into the PCB (except the Rs and Cs!) , since I left some out the last session. Had the power components on the B.cu so that everything would be neater! Plus, they weren't needed on the front side anyway.

![Screenshot 2026-11-13 at 6.17.29 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/9c8f0f10c386742ac2be474381fa51d0adf9fc35695a28f3eae18c2f6fc99e9a.png)
After that, I focused on the power components (yeah did not expect how long it would eventually take...) Firstly, I wasn't even sure where to put the resistors. Yeah.
So, I had to pull out the good ol datasheet. Didn't think I'd have to use it again... But yes it was very useful.

![Screenshot 2026-11-13 at 6.24.23 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/cf06c9837667f20ee64d7ddd8f9f7768ff11f97544fda98a52e034d89e118f1c.png)
After referring back and forth for who knows how long, I finally finally got the resistors to the best placement I could get. So now every component is in the PCB woohoo!

![Screenshot 2026-11-13 at 6.29.15 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/df559cc557d0cd8952800a5118625b9a0cf94bd07e04a0771de7ec7d35f66a68.png)
Ran the DRC and um..... Too many violations? Yeah so I googled it and apparentlyyyy it should be fine. Hopefully. Because yeah I ended up ignoring that + the clearance violations since I needed the slide switch and usb to be really near the edge.

![Screenshot 2026-11-13 at 3.13.36 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/e9b584115a4ff941d296f820a99f387e05672dc0c2f129fed0b99154afddefb3.png)
I focused on completing the design of the PCB for this session so yay done after!

### 2026-11-12: 12/11: ROUTING TIME!

**6h**

12/11: ROUTING TIME!

Oohohohoh routing routing routing, the big boss. This one really took a toll on me TT^TT since there was so much to route for this project. (So far, they've been pretty simple since I'd just been following the guide).

![Screenshot 2026-11-13 at 3.31.30 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/7a54d065b7e224184944a46735f85a5503b397ada03d5d1d2c76104a25fcf84e.png)
Before starting, I made some additions to the board setup; making the track width for the power net class thicker so that more current for the power can flow through and it won't overheat too easily!

![Screenshot 2026-11-13 at 4.10.28 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/81636b0d34d84db2c7da8a78a8948805a368df57500cc1c7256f8ff596b7124f.png)
Starting off the routing, which I briefly forgot which key to press (x) but it was easy after the tiny refresher, I connected the pads on the key switches. Did the rows on F.cu and the columns on B.cu. Left some unconnected since there was a lot going on at the cluster of power components. This was the easiest part of routing. :(

![Screenshot 2026-11-13 at 4.27.10 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/229dff0057ea2c81f311fb7d11bff0b42777bf51f30b65dce01d2c5314ee86be.png)
After the key switches, I moved on to route as much as I could at the FPC connector yay! I learned that I had to make the routes as close as possible to leave enough space for more routing (experience!) I also tried to route all of the main column and row switches to the RPi pins. I definitely need to work on my routing looks wise, but its a lot better than my first few projects ;>

![Screenshot 2026-11-13 at 4.49.15 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/8e507fa567a24fc9b04687c0ee0c0a5b4802f109bc57c96644c053283e87f833.png)
More, more, more routing!! Got a lot more done here, and tried to connect all of the GND pins first (which I would later deeply regret...) since I thought hey there are the most number of gnd pins let's do them first then
And these actually took quite long too :<

![CyberdeckieSS20](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/3ea2d931088a8d55f28ba1d65149810893201b53b867f784a2cdfc328371947f.webp)
Oh gosh ran into so many problems with this project. For this screenshot above, I was really frustrated because I couldn't seem to move the track anywhere. Literally. Apparently, it was because the track was too thick since it was a power pad and couldn't move past the gap between the R1 and hole. Omg. I  was stuck staring at this after putting it off for as long as I could already and just couldn't figure it out. Yeah so what I did in the end was creating pre-defined sizes for the track and switching to that instead. It worked like a charm.

![Screenshot 2026-11-13 at 6.38.53 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/430d1424650820eefba7e46754f5234831a90c2b6e5a0f7a83b2ef625cb0f8f0.png)
Kinda forgot to take more screenshots so this is already after quite a while but some context here anyway: When I was trying to route all of the pins, especially those at the power components, I couldn't route them because they were all blocked by the multiple gnd tracks... It was so so so annoying but I still worked my way around it somehow(?) although it was really messy. However, there were 1 or 2 pins that just couldn't move because it was blocked by everything around and I couldn't swap it to F.cu either cos there was just not enough space. So, I googled a little here and there and of course I realised I didn't need to connect all of the gnd pads because there's a thing called gnd pour (week 1...) sigh so yeah I painstakingly removed all of the gnd connections to make sure I could route everything else first. And it worked so so so much better. Yes, it does still look messy, but at least they connect!

### 2026-11-13: 13/11: Last last session to really complete the PCB

**2.5h**

13/11: Last last session to really complete the PCB

![Screenshot 2026-11-13 at 6.46.24 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/151417c05c34a8951801b8f0d5136700d057917ced42da1553499471e9bce7ba.png)
After routing what I thought was needed (excluding gnd) I went ahead with the ERC and found a few pads still unconnected so I went ahead and did that until only the gnd pads were left so that I could finally do the gnd pour.

![Screenshot 2026-11-13 at 8.19.22 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/75ccd6034afeb4bad7bae7f89e180bbbc1a9ca74338ca54d7b111a803e6a3b65.png)
Didn't take enough screenshots again but anyway. Forgot how to do a gnd pour so thank you youtube! After the gnd pour, a few gnd pads were still unrouted so  I went ahead and routed those manually and everything was routed and good!

After seeing the final PCB, I felt a huge sense of accomplishment!

![Screenshot 2026-11-14 at 12.04.04 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/dd0e4c20a149db521e879c6689865e6e7ccab9500d767b99bfe2ac742a2bbf6d.png)
But of course, you aren't done with your PCB without your silkscreen art :D
However, since I was short on time, I decided to just stick with my cyberdeckie name, year, and also labels for the LEDs for future reference. I wish I did more for the art, but there wasn't much space to begin with anyway so it was okay
